findings.title: float: right on .small-action button no longer applies once .small-action is a flex container
findings.body: This PR makes `.small-action` a flex container via `@include flexbox()`. Browsers ignore `float` on flex items, so the `button { float: right; }` rule (and `float: left` on `.topic-avatar`) has no effect anymore. The button will sit directly after `.small-action-desc` instead of being pushed to the right edge, which is a visible layout regression. Add `margin-left: auto` (or a high `order` plus auto margin) to the button to keep the right alignment.

findings.title: align-items mixin passes modern values to legacy properties that use a different value set
findings.body: The mixin emits the same `$alignment` for `-webkit-box-align`, `-ms-flex-align` and `align-items`. The legacy properties use `start`/`end` where the modern syntax uses `flex-start`/`flex-end`. The two current callers pass `center` and `baseline`, which work everywhere. Any future `@include align-items(flex-start)` will silently produce invalid declarations in the legacy-prefixed browsers this mixin exists to support. The values should be mapped before being written to the legacy properties.

findings.title: `-ms-align-items` is not a real property
findings.body: IE10 only supports `-ms-flex-align`; no `-ms-align-items` property exists. This line is dead output in every compiled rule that uses the mixin and should be removed.
